claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr and CoCrFeMnNi are examples of equiatomic or nearly equiatomic five-component high-entropy alloys.
The proposed nanoparticles initially have a random solid-solution structure.
Thermal annealing between 300 K and 1300 K will induce structural evolution in these nanoparticles.
Elevated-temperature nanoparticles will develop chemical short-range order and ordered clusters.
The short-range order and ordered clusters in the nanoparticles are induced by their surfaces.
Surface-energy minimization drives the formation of short-range order and ordered clusters in the nanoparticle regime.
Reduced configurational entropy in nanoparticles promotes ordered-cluster formation.
Ordered clusters may include B2 phases.
Bulk high-entropy alloys rely on high configurational entropy for structural stability.
Bulk high-entropy alloys exhibit sluggish diffusion that contributes to their stability.
Surface energy dominates the behavior of high-entropy alloy nanoparticles because of their high surface-to-volume ratio.
Short-range order reduces lattice distortion or atomic displacement.
The reduction in lattice distortion caused by short-range order increases local atomic mobility.
Reduced surface configurational entropy lowers the thermodynamic barrier to phase separation.
Surface-induced ordering will accelerate atomic diffusion and grain growth relative to bulk samples.
Short-range ordering will increase nanoparticle thermal conductivity by 10–15%.
Nanoparticles will undergo phase separation earlier than bulk samples at the same temperature.
Surface diffusion pathways make the sluggish-diffusion effect less pronounced in nanoparticles.
Bulk HfNbTaTiZr remains a single-phase BCC alloy up to 1300 K with minimal phase separation because of configurational entropy and sluggish diffusion.
Particles larger than 100 nm will behave like bulk material rather than showing surface-dominated ordering.

contradictions.description: The experiment anneals samples only at 1000 K, but the falsification rule requires determining whether they remain stable up to 1300 K; the stated design cannot directly evaluate that criterion.
